summary: Ryojun Okubo (1928–1999) worked in Buddhist studies. He studied under Morito Ninomiya and held a position as department head at Taisho University, attested between 1978 and 1984.

Ryokei Kaginushi (1926–2005) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He taught Nobuyoshi Yamabe and served as a professor in the Faculty of Letters and university professor at Otani University, attested between 1978 and 1993.
Ryoken Nawa specializes in Buddhist studies. He served as a commissioned researcher at Kyoto Koka Women's University (attested 2015) and held a post at Osaka University (attested 2020).
Ryoko Mochizuki (born 1933) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at the University of Tokyo until 1963 and served as a lecturer at Rissho University, attested in 1972 and 1983.

Ryomin Akizuki (1921–1999) worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1946 to 1950, held a post at Saitama Medical University from circa 1972 to 1991, and taught Makio Takemura.

Ryosaburo Sakaki (1872–1946) worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at Third Higher School and the University of Tokyo (graduating 1895). He lectured at Ryukoku University (1897) and held professorships at Third Higher School (1899) and Kyoto University (1908).

Ryosei Fukuda (1937–2021) specialized in Buddhist studies, earning his doctorate at Toyo University. A professor and later professor emeritus at Taisho University, he held leadership roles at Chisan Denpōin, Chisan Kangakukai, Chisan Senshū Gakuin, and the Kawasaki Daishi Institute.

Ryoshin Nakao (born 1952) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University. He held positions at the Soto Zen Religious Studies Institute, the Research Institute of Soto Studies, and served as a professor at Hanazono University (attested 1998).

Ryosho Hayashi (1927–2008) worked in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. Educated at Taisho University and Tokyo Metropolitan University, he served at Taisho University as professor, dean of the Faculty of Literature, and university president (1990–1994).

Ryosho Nakamura (1927–2013) specialized in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Seventh Higher School, Tohoku University under Ensho Kanakura, and Rissho University. From circa 1968 to 1998, he served as a professor at The International University of Kagoshima.

Ryosho Tanaka (1933–2016) was a Buddhist studies scholar educated at Komazawa University. He served as professor at Ryukoku University and held numerous roles at Komazawa University from 1962 onward, including professor, dean, museum director, professor emeritus, and university president (2009).

Ryoshu Kouda works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Seitatsu Matsunami and held researcher posts at Taisho University (attested 1998) and the Hasegawa Buddhist Cultural Institute (attested 2006).

Ryoshu Michihata (1903–1993) worked in Buddhist studies and Sinology. After studying at Otani University (~1925–1928), he held a post there from circa 1930 to 1969, and later served as professor at Kyoto Koka Women's University (~1969–1980).

Ryoshu Misaki (1921–2010) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Waseda University from circa 1941 to 1948 and later served there as professor emeritus during his tenure from circa 1960 to 1992.

Ryoshun Okubo (born 1954) specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at Waseda University (~1974–1984), where he became Professor of Sino-Japanese Buddhism around 2002 and taught Shigeki Moro. He was also director of Taimon Kenkyūkai (attested 2007).
Ryosuke Furui is a scholar in Indology and history and archaeology. He completed his PhD at Jawaharlal Nehru University in 2007 and held a post at the University of Tokyo (attested 2011).

Ryota Nakamura works in Buddhist studies. Attested in 2015, he pursued doctoral studies and served as a graduate student researcher at Toyo University, while also working as a researcher at the Shinran Buddhist Center.

Ryotai Hatani (1883–1974) was a Buddhist studies scholar who taught Gadjin M. Nagao and Ryogon Fukuhara. He served as professor emeritus at Ryukoku University (circa 1920–1956) and held a post at Kyoto University from 1929 to 1943.
Ryotai Shibuya was a scholar in the field of Buddhist studies. He completed his education at Tendai Sect University and Kokugakuin University.

Ryoun Yamada (born 1940) works in Buddhist studies. He studied under Yamada Koun and at Harvard Business School. After corporate careers at Mitsubishi Bank, Tokyu Railways, and Itoki Corporation, he became leader of Sanbo Zen in 2004.
